description:
FILED s439 (Fable) from s438 ask 10.  Five changes in a row (#453, #365, #454,
#455, #435) were emission-IDENTICAL over all four populations (corpus-diff 111,
lib 22, cpan 402, perl t/ 604) and were guarded only by `both_agree` rows plus
an inverse run on a worktree -- the s371 rule working as intended, and also
five real bugs living in shapes no population contains.

RULED: a small corpus -- `Pl/t/shapes/*.pl` (or `docs/shapes/`), ONE file per
family (operand grammar, sub heads, bareword handles, interpolation,
glob/readline, punctuation arrays) -- that `tools/corpus-diff.pl` and
`tools/emission-ab.pl --list` accept as a POPULATION, so that a change which
is identical over the four real populations is still A/B'd over the shapes
that exist only to exercise the grammar.  It does NOT replace the rows (a row
asserts perl's answer; an A/B asserts only "unchanged") and it must not grow
into a second test suite.  ADMISSION RULE: a shape that moved a fix in some
session and occurs in no population -- the s438 guard files
(user-unary-01.t, imported-term-01.t, sig-param-shadow-01.t,
punct-array-glob-01.t, utf8-source-01.t) are the seed; lift their perl
snippets out as files, do not duplicate the rows.

Bar: the tools accept the population (a `--shapes` flag or the list file);
`tools/corpus-diff.pl` prints it as its own line (never mixed into the
111-file IDENTICAL verdict); one session, Opus; no emission change.
subject: A SHAPES corpus for the emission A/B: deliberately-awkward files that exist only to exercise grammar no real population contains (ask 10 of s438, ruled s439 YES)
